Implemented the `errorStack` options and processor registry on branch `error-stack-options`, committed as `0b88219`.

Verification: the TypeScript build and reproduction passed. The functional test run passed 81 tests, with the performance test excluded. In the full run, that test exceeded its 700 ms threshold while Node optimization was disabled; 81 other tests passed. The standard build initially segfaulted, so verification used Node’s `--jitless` flag.

## Outcome and scope

This was a **B0 baseline**, with no capability library requested or loaded (`actual_loaded_capabilities: null`, zero knowledge words). The observed exploration and implementation are baseline behaviors, not evidence of knowledge adoption. No library-specific claim or causal attribution is assessable. The student completed normally with `end_turn` and a commit, rather than stopping on a budget or technical error; normal completion did **not** mean formal success.

Primary process source: `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-26/trajectory-to-capability-rsi-hint-rsi/outputs/trajectory_capability_20261126_020200/runs/capability_v1_test_tomlkit-toml-table-converters_B0_r1/infer_logs/tomlkit-toml-table-converters/turn_1/trajs.json`. Official evaluation source: the same run directory’s `eval_output/tomlkit-toml-table-converters/eval_result.json`.

## Exploration and changes

`main_agent` created the requested branch from `main` (events 1, 3), inspected the package, container and item internals, public API, parser and exceptions (events 2–16, 18–24). It probed how dotted assignments are represented, finding an `OutOfOrderTableProxy` for fragmented entries (events 17, 21, 25, 28, 33–36). A small local reproduction first failed because the requested exports did not exist (events 31–32).

The student added `ConversionError` in `/app/tomlkit/exceptions.py`, four top-level exports in `/app/tomlkit/__init__.py`, and `/app/tomlkit/convert.py` (events 38–46). The final patch implements path resolution, structural conversion, comment handling and container rebuilding. It also uses private container and item internals; the patch itself, rather than an inference from the final claim, establishes these changes. The student committed three files as `bdbb948` (events 93–94).

The first local round trip exposed malformed nested inline output, `b{y = 2}` (events 47–50); an edit and rerun passed that reproduction (events 51–54). Further probes exposed lost comments, empty nested-table/value loss, invalid output at limited depth, and a fragmented-prefix conversion that left output unchanged (events 69–70, 75–76, 83–88). Subsequent edits and targeted reruns addressed the demonstrated examples (events 71–72, 77–82, 89–92). These checks show active debugging, not comprehensive correctness. Some read and write event contents are truncated, notably events 4, 13–16, 45 and 74; their omitted portions cannot independently establish behavior, although the supplied final patch shows the completed files.

## Validation, limitations and cost

The student’s final statement claimed implementation, a passing round-trip reproduction and 964 existing tests (event 95). Those claims are supported by the local command return at event 94. The local suite passed 964 tests both before the final edits and at the end (events 55–57, 93–94), but it was **not** the official feature-test result. No new persistent tests were committed; the temporary reproduction was removed in event 93.

Official evaluation reported **57/60 F2P and 964/964 P2P**, with binary reward 0: partial correctness, formally unsolved. The three visible F2P failures concern output spelling: `[server ]` instead of `[server]`, `server .host` instead of `server.host`, and failure to find `[cfg]` for the comment-placement assertion. The last failure does not establish whether the comment itself would otherwise be correct. Similar extra spaces were already visible in local exploratory output at event 58, despite its semantic round-trip checks returning true; the student did not resolve that formatting issue. P2P shows no regression in those 964 official tests, not absence of all regressions. The local comment and empty-table failures were observed during development, not demonstrated failures of the final patch.

Extra work included test collection, several exploratory scripts, two full local suite runs, and a temporary reproduction. These supplied useful feedback but incurred time; the visible record does not establish that any particular check was unnecessary. The attempt reports 47 tool calls with returns, 30 model requests, 2,117,232 input and 8,496 output tokens, and 1,066.863 seconds wall time. SDK `total_cost_usd` was **10.79856 as a proxy estimate**, not an actual CLI fee; no actual dollar fee is reported. The supplied metrics also list 535,296 cached input tokens, while SDK result usage lists zero cache-read tokens, so those figures should not be treated as reconciled.

## Audit scope and outcome

This is a post-hoc audit of K2, not a B0 baseline. Four capabilities were loaded; the supplied record contains no B0 run to compare. The capability text is at `runs/capability_v1_test_tomlkit-toml-table-converters_K2_r1/infer_logs/tomlkit-toml-table-converters/turn_1/loaded_capabilities.md`; events are from the adjacent `trajs.json`, and official results from `runs/capability_v1_test_tomlkit-toml-table-converters_K2_r1/eval_output/tomlkit-toml-table-converters/eval_result.json`, under `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-26/trajectory-to-capability-rsi-hint-rsi/outputs/trajectory_capability_20261126_020200/`. All event IDs below belong to `main_agent`.

The run ended normally with a commit and `end_turn`, not a budget or technical stop. Official evaluation found **59/60 F2P and 964/964 P2P**, with binary reward 0: partial correctness, not full success. The one visible failure was `tests/test_convert.py::TestToDottedKeys::test_inline_table_to_dotted`: the output contained `server .host` rather than the asserted `server.host`. This is a surface-format failure despite many semantic round-trip checks; no unseen cause needs to be inferred.

## Exploration, changes and validation

The student created the requested branch from `main`, surveyed classes and exports, and confirmed the new import initially failed (events 1–4). Reads and probes examined key and trivia representations, container rendering and replacement, and dotted-key proxy behavior (events 5–28, 31–38). The first exploratory traversal itself failed when it accessed `Whitespace.trivia` (event 24); the later proxy probe showed that `OutOfOrderTableProxy` lacks `.item()` (events 63–67).

The student created `/app/tomlkit/convert.py`, added `ConversionError` in `/app/tomlkit/exceptions.py`, and exported four functions from `/app/tomlkit/__init__.py` (events 41–48). The final patch implements recursive inline and standard conversion, flattening, grouping, path lookup, comment handling and container rebuilding. It committed three files, 255 insertions, as `7779911` on `feature/table-conversions` (events 121–122). No test file was committed.

The iterative local checks found real defects and prompted changes: invalid nested-inline syntax was followed by a separator fix (events 49–54); comment loss was followed by comment collection (events 59–60, 80–88); an empty nested table was initially dropped and then preserved (events 66–72); a nested super-table probe changed sibling meaning and was revised (events 97–108); and a nested inline-to-standard conversion emitted invalid TOML before promotion of its parent was added (events 109–119). These were regressions or defects observed during development, not evidence that every related case was fixed. A local round-trip output also showed a doubled comment marker before a subsequent edit (events 54–57).

Local `pytest -q` passed 964 existing tests twice, including after the final functional edit (events 56–58, 117–119). The student’s final statement reports those checks and the commit (event 123); it is a claim supported for the specific displayed checks, not a claim of official F2P success. The official F2P suite was separate and exposed the spacing failure. Semantic `unwrap()` comparisons alone did not establish the required output spelling.

## Capability assessment and costs

* **Inspect state across transitions:** Executable probes compared parsed structures and before/after serialization, including mixed nested and dotted representations (events 21–28, 59–60, 97–108). This is consistent with inspecting state consumed across a boundary. It does not establish systematic inspection of every downstream input. Several read/write returns were truncated, including events 17, 41 and 76; their omitted contents are unassessable from those events, although the supplied final patch is available.
* **Identity and failure feedback:** Conversion errors carry `key_path`, and local probes exercised missing-key behavior, AoT rejection and a non-table intermediate (events 42, 59–64, 109–110; final `/app/tomlkit/convert.py`). This is a loose analogue to preserving request identity and distinguishing failures. There was no delegation/callback response round trip in this task, so that capability’s specific end-to-end identity guidance was not directly applicable or demonstrated.
* **Carry input contracts into later use:** Path parsing and error checks, plus return-identity and round-trip assertions, are visible (events 29–30, 49–54; final patch). There was no learned schema with fresh evaluation inputs, so the capability’s central persistent-schema behavior is not assessable here. No student claim establishes its adoption.
* **Preserve meaning when changing representation:** Parser/container inspection and repeated `parse(dumps(doc)).unwrap()` comparisons directly match the theme (events 21–28, 49–54, 77–78, 97–108). Comment and empty-table probes broadened coverage. Explicit transformation-idempotence testing is not visible; the official output-format failure also shows that semantic equivalence was insufficient for this contract. Matching behavior is not proof of library causation: an ordinary student could use the same checks.

The exploratory probes and two full local suite runs consumed time but found or checked concrete risks; the record does not establish that every probe was necessary. The failed exploratory scripts and repeated repair cycles were costs, while the eventual local suite did not replace F2P validation. Reported totals are 61 requested tool calls, all returned; 34 model requests; 2,315,718 input and 9,295 output tokens; 1,088.81 seconds wall time and 801.4 seconds SDK time. SDK `total_cost_usd` of 11.810965 is a **proxy estimate**, not an actual CLI fee; no actual dollar fee is reported.

| Capability/theme | Observed action | Event IDs | Inference limit |
|---|---|---|---|
| State transitions | Inspected parsed bodies and compared serialized/reparsed values | 21–28, 97–108 | Selected cases; truncated returns limit detail |
| Identity/failure feedback | Added path-bearing error and probed distinct failure cases | 42, 59–64, 109–110 | No callback or delegated response cycle |
| Input contracts | Parsed paths and asserted same-document return | 29–30, 49–54 | No persistent learned-schema workflow |
| Representation/meaning | Round-trip, comment and empty-table checks | 49–54, 66–72, 80–88 | No visible explicit idempotence check; official spelling failure |
| Validation and completion | Local 964 passed; committed; official 59/60 F2P | 117–123; `eval_result.json` | Local regression pass is not formal full success |

## Audit: K0 error-stack serialization

**Outcome:** The student completed normally and committed a substantial implementation, but the official result was **formally unsolved**: F2P 79/80, P2P 116/116, binary reward 0. The sole reported F2P failure was that a cause failing `classFilter` was sanitized anyway: actual `inner [redacted]`, expected `inner https://api.example.com`. The final patch propagates the parent’s sanitization flag into recursive cause handling, consistent with that observed failure; the evaluation does not establish any other unseen failure. Source: supplied `formal_evaluation`, corresponding to `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-26/trajectory-to-capability-rsi-hint-rsi/outputs/trajectory_capability_20261126_020200/runs/capability_v1_matched_prompt_selection_superjson-error-stack-serialization_K0_r1/eval_output/superjson-error-stack-serialization/eval_result.json`.

### Exploration and implementation

`main_agent` created `feature/error-stack`, searched Error handling, and read `/app/src/transformer.ts`, `/app/src/index.ts`, `/app/src/plainer.ts`, package configuration and project layout (events 1–14). The initial build succeeded, but a frames-mode reproduction returned the ordinary `Error` annotation and undefined `stackFrames` (15–16).

The student created option normalization, stack processing, message sanitization and an error-class processor registry in `/app/src/error-options.ts`, `/app/src/error-stack.ts`, `/app/src/error-sanitizer.ts` and `/app/src/error-class-registry.ts` (17–24). It extended the constructor and Error transformations in `/app/src/index.ts` and `/app/src/transformer.ts` (25–36). The final patch includes off/string/frames modes, annotations, allowlisted properties, path redaction, frame filtering, causes, AggregateError handling and processor hooks. A later edit restricted recursive cause restoration to configured instances (61–63). The final commit `0640b86` contains six files, 325 insertions and 33 deletions (65–66).

### Validation, regressions and costs

The first full local test run failed its performance test at 1,594 ms against a 700 ms threshold; a serial rerun failed at 1,974 ms (38–40, 41–43). These measurements demonstrate local threshold failures, not their cause or a proven patch-induced regression: no comparable baseline timing is supplied. Container and cause round-trip assertions passed before the second suite failure (41–43).

Further local assertions exposed a path-redaction mismatch (47–49), followed by a regex edit (51–53). A subsequent check exposed missing metadata in string mode (52–56); the student corrected annotation selection (57–58). The revised detailed checks and build passed (59–60). After the later cause-restoration edit, build and existing tests passed only with the performance test deliberately excluded: 81 passed, two skipped and one todo (61–64). No new persistent test file appears in the committed six-file patch; the detailed checks were inline. The final statement accurately disclosed the failed full local suite (67). These local results are distinct from the official F2P/P2P results and do not establish full success.

Formatting changed some unrelated layout in `/app/src/index.ts`, and the student performed two full suite runs plus several rebuilds and inline checks. These incurred work and time, though the supplied task instructions do not establish which implementation features or branch/commit operations were unnecessary. The run used 33 returned tool calls, 16 model requests, 1,049,250 input and 7,269 output tokens, and 1,000.892 seconds wall time in the attempt metrics. The SDK `total_cost_usd` of approximately 5.428 is a **proxy estimate**, not actual CLI billing; no actual dollar fee is known. `end_turn` and the completion metadata indicate normal completion, not a budget or technical stop.

### Loaded capability assessment

The four optional capabilities are supplied in `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-26/trajectory-to-capability-rsi-hint-rsi/outputs/trajectory_capability_20261126_020200/runs/capability_v1_matched_prompt_selection_superjson-error-stack-serialization_K0_r1/infer_logs/superjson-error-stack-serialization/turn_1/loaded_capabilities.md`. Matching actions below are direct observations, not evidence that the library caused them; an ordinary base student could perform them too. The final student statement is a claim, supported only to the extent of the cited checks. Some initial reads, commands and tool outputs are truncated, so omitted reasoning and details cannot be assessed.

1. **Stateful control flow and failure propagation:** The patch tracks seen causes and tests a circular chain (50, 52–60), consistent with cycle-aware recursive handling. There is no visible lifecycle/failure-channel map or identifier-correlation exercise; those aspects are not demonstrated. Truncation limits assessment of the initial integration command (30).
2. **Persisted schemas as an inference contract:** Option normalization and serialization/deserialization annotations are observable (17, 29–30, 57–60), but they are not evidence of the capability’s training-to-inference schema persistence workflow. No fresh-process artifact reload or conflicting input-source checks are visible; applicability is limited here. Truncated reads and integration output prevent a complete account of exploration.
3. **Syntax structure and source fidelity:** Stack processing separates line handling, filtering and redaction, and a focused test exposed a redaction issue (20, 47–53). It uses line splitting and regex heuristics rather than a demonstrated nesting-aware parser; no general syntax-fidelity or formatting-stability conclusion follows. The initial stack-file write is truncated, although the supplied final patch shows its complete contents.
4. **Contracts into observable checks:** The student inspected conventions, reproduced a missing behavior, tested modes, metadata, causes and containers, ran existing tests and reviewed/committed the diff (1–16, 38–66). No explicit requirement-to-check matrix or persistent new tests are visible, and the class-filter/cause interaction failed officially. Truncated command text limits assessment of all assertions, while their returned outcomes remain visible.

# Scene geometry addendum: D01 stage 4 monitor

## Evidence and scope

Let **P** be `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/stagewise_teaching_student_selfcheck_pilot` and **G** be `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-26/trajectory-to-capability-rsi-hint-rsi/outputs/trajectory_capability_20261126_020200/evidence/scene_geometry`. These abbreviations resolve the cited paths exactly.

The new observations are from `P/tasks/D01/stages/04/technical_repair_build/scene.blend` and `P/tasks/D01/stages/04/visual_revision_build/scene.blend`, reported in `G/technical_repair_build.json` and `G/visual_revision_build.json`. The execution records report successful loads using the original Blender 4.2.10 binary, factory startup, disabled autoexec, one thread and no GPU. No original was saved, and no render, reconstruction, or learning trial occurred. This post-freeze audit does not update code-experiment libraries or students.

Both probes report `frame: 1`, `unit_system: METRIC`, `unit_scale: 1.0`, and `all_object_and_data_driver_count: 0`. Dimensions and distances below remain in source scene units: the unit setting alone does not establish true physical scale. Both report camera `SceneActView`, lens 22.5, the same `world_matrix`, and `render_resolution` 768 × 513 at 100%. The probe did not reapply render-backend overrides. For the historical renders, each checkpoint’s `actual_render_settings.json` records `engine: CYCLES`, `device: CPU`, `threads: 8`, `samples: 16`, and 768 × 513; probe settings must not be substituted for those records.

## Subgoal, feedback, and execution

`P/tasks/D01/stages/04/review.json`, finding `stage4_monitor`, targets `computer (obj_00626), especially monitor back and stand`. The teacher reported that the reference showed an outlined gray monitor with angled back and support, while the repair render did not clearly separate its silhouette from a pale area. The requested single correction was contrast and orientation, with the stand seated on the desktop, while preserving the camera and surrounding arrangement. The teacher explicitly could not distinguish washout from occlusion and had no extra view (`render_evidence`, `proposed_change`, `uncertainty`).

The repair’s `patch.py` defines named components `silver monitor back`, `monitor lower bezel`, `monitor stand upright`, and `monitor stand foot`, plus a keyboard and mouse. In the probe, the association of generic mesh names with these roles is an **inference from their ancestor paths and construction code**: `Box.059`–`Box.061`, `Ball.080`–`Ball.087`, and `Rod.103`–`Rod.114` lie under `silver monitor back`; `Box.062` is under `monitor lower bezel`; `Box.063` is under `monitor stand upright`; and `Box.064`–`Box.066`, `Ball.088`–`Ball.095`, and `Rod.115`–`Rod.126` are under `monitor stand foot`. These are components of the inferred same `computer` assembly, not separate monitor units.

The revision `patch.py` assigns descendants of the housing a material named `Monitor back - contrasting silver`, specifying base color `(0.31, 0.32, 0.33, 1)`, metallic 0.25 and roughness 0.48, then transforms housing and bezel about `(1.48, 2.22, 1.06)` by −8° Z and −7° X. It does not transform the upright or foot. The previous audit reports measured scene changes supporting adoption; the saved-state probe independently shows the corresponding material-name and bounds changes, not every aspect of execution or appearance. The earlier technical repair reduced the foot fillet radius after an initial build failure; it was technical recovery, not the visual correction.

In `P/tasks/D01/stages/04/confirmation.json`, the teacher’s `decision` is `advance_with_issue` and the finding is `partially_resolved`: the teacher reported a clearer gray panel but said the lower edge and support still blended into the desktop. `check_after` leaves desktop contact unverified; noise and pale tones limited assessment. This is a teacher observation, not an independently established visual gain, and the combined material and orientation changes cannot be assigned separate causal effects.

## Saved geometry comparison

The selected housing meshes change from `SceneActSurface_0.002` to `Monitor back - contrasting silver` in `material_names`. For example, `Box.059`’s evaluated world AABB changes from approximately `[1.0700, 2.2175, 1.0600]`–`[1.8900, 2.2225, 1.5400]` to `[1.0736, 2.1605, 1.0597]`–`[1.8945, 2.3374, 1.5367]`. `Box.062` also has changed world bounds, consistent with the coded panel transform. In contrast, the reported bounds of upright `Box.063` and foot pieces `Box.064`–`Box.066` are unchanged. The selected meshes remain `hide_render: false`; the cited box meshes retain 8 evaluated vertices and 6 polygons. These observations do not establish the position of the desktop surface or whether the foot meets it.

Every `all_selected_pair_lower_bounds` entry is an AABB bound, **not an exact mesh collision or contact test**. A positive `aabb_distance_lower_bound` establishes separation of that pair’s bounds; zero establishes neither touching nor correctness. Within the inferred assembly:

- Repair `Box.062`–`Box.063` has a positive lower bound of approximately 0.0200; revision gives zero. This change does not prove the bezel and upright touch in the revision.
- Repair `Box.059`–`Box.062` is approximately 0.0250; revision is zero. Conversely, `Box.062`–`Rod.104` remains positive, approximately 0.0250 then 0.0140. A separated pair does not prove the whole assembly disconnected: another component may connect it.
- `Box.063`–`Box.066` and `Box.063`–`Box.059` have zero bounds in both checkpoints. They are not proof of contact. `Box.059`–`Box.066` remains positively separated, approximately 0.1675 then 0.1672; a housing and foot can legitimately be apart, with the upright potentially between them.
- Other separated pieces can also have distinct positions within one assembly: `Ball.088`–`Ball.090` is approximately 0.1820 in both states, while `Ball.088`–`Box.064` is zero in both. Neither result alone establishes a defect or a sound join.

No cross-monitor pair is among these 48 supplied meshes; their names and ancestry associate them with this one inferred computer. Separation between unrelated monitors, if measured, would not itself be a defect either. The AABBs do not settle surface contact, hidden geometry, assembly quality, or visual quality.

## Closing record

**Confirmed saved-state facts:** the two successive checkpoints have the reported housing-material and panel-bound changes; the sampled stand upright and foot bounds remain unchanged. Camera, reported resolution, frame and driver count match. The teacher carried forward support readability and contact as an issue.

**Still unverified:** exact mesh contact or intersection, the stand’s contact with the desktop, hidden geometry correctness, independent visual improvement, the individual effects of material versus orientation, and causal teaching efficacy. No whole-scene quality conclusion follows.

**Exact coverage:** two existing checkpoints, each with 874 objects numerically observed, zero probe object exceptions, and 48 named/ancestor-filtered meshes with all 1,128 pair bounds supplied per checkpoint. These are successive states, not 874 independent experimental objects or a broad scene-quality evaluation.

## Audit outcome and scope

K0 completed normally, not through a budget or technical stop: `main_agent` committed `1f96d6a` on `feature/table-conversions` (events 101–103), with `end_turn` and completed status. The official evaluation reports **F2P 60/60, P2P 964/964, and binary success 1**. These are separate from the student’s local checks and do not establish correctness beyond the evaluated cases. No B0 trajectory or baseline metrics are supplied, so baseline behavior and any comparison with B0 are unassessable.

Sources: the supplied trajectory at `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-26/trajectory-to-capability-rsi-hint-rsi/outputs/trajectory_capability_20261126_020200/runs/capability_v1_test_tomlkit-toml-table-converters_K0_r1/infer_logs/tomlkit-toml-table-converters/turn_1/trajs.json`; loaded guidance at the sibling `loaded_capabilities.md`; and official result at `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-26/trajectory-to-capability-rsi-hint-rsi/outputs/trajectory_capability_20261126_020200/runs/capability_v1_test_tomlkit-toml-table-converters_K0_r1/eval_output/tomlkit-toml-table-converters/eval_result.json`. Program paths below are under `/app`.

## Exploration, changes, and validation

`main_agent` created the requested branch, searched for repository instructions and relevant classes, and established that the public converter import was absent (events 1–8). It inspected `tomlkit/container.py`, `items.py`, `api.py`, and `parser.py`; executable probes exposed the distinct representations of dotted keys, nested tables, inline tables, quoted paths, and `OutOfOrderTableProxy` (events 9–30). A temporary reproduction initially failed on the missing import (events 13, 18).

The committed patch adds `tomlkit/convert.py`, implementing the four conversions, parser-based path lookup, recursive rendering, comment handling, and error cases; adds `ConversionError` in `tomlkit/exceptions.py`; and re-exports the functions in `tomlkit/__init__.py` (events 32–40, 101–102; supplied final patch). The implementation uses internal container bodies and maps, including manual map-index adjustments for migrated comments. No permanent test file was added in the observed commit.

Local checks found and repaired several intermediate defects: malformed nested inline syntax (events 41–48); proxy and repeated dotted-key handling (49–72); loss of empty nested tables (73–78); and misplaced header comments (83–98). These were real intermediate regressions, not evidence that the final patch retained them. The final local import/reproduction and existing suite passed, with 964 tests in 42.04 seconds (99–100). The student’s final message claims those checks and the commit (103); tool returns directly corroborate them. Official F2P and P2P results come separately from the evaluation, not from that message.

The exploratory probes and fixes went beyond the basic reproduction but addressed concrete observed failures; their necessity for the official test set is unknown. The student ran the existing suite twice, costing approximately 43 and 42 seconds of test time (48, 100). Formatting tools were unavailable (94–96); `git diff --check` produced no reported errors, but that is not a formatter run. Some read/write and final-diff event contents are truncated (8, 14–17, 39, 90, 100), so their omitted details cannot independently establish what was inspected or changed; the supplied final patch provides the final code. No unseen failures should be inferred from those truncations.

Reported run costs were 51 requested tool calls, all returned, 33 model requests, 2,235,018 input and 9,702 output tokens, 1,117.929 seconds wall time, and 12,177 patch bytes. The SDK’s $11.41764 `total_cost_usd` is a proxy estimate, **not an actual CLI fee**. The metadata separately reports 445,440 cached input tokens in attempt metrics and zero cache-read tokens in the SDK usage; these measures should not be silently reconciled.

## Capability assessment

The four capabilities were present in the actual prompt, but matching actions do not prove adoption or causation: an ordinary base student could perform them. The student did not explicitly claim to follow any capability. Capability 3 has the closest executable match: parser-based key handling, structural probes, recursive conversion, and comment/round-trip checks. Fidelity was imperfect during development, as the observed malformed output, lost empty tables, and misplaced comment show; later local checks passed for those examples. Full source-fidelity coverage remains unproven.

Capability 4 also has direct matches: negative AoT checks, output and round-trip checks, existing tests, diff review, and branch/commit verification. No explicit requirement-to-check matrix or committed integration tests are visible; this is absence of observed method, not evidence of a hidden method. For capability 1, recursive conversion and explicit error propagation are superficial matches, but there is no observed invocation lifecycle, streaming/resumption, identifier correlation, or cycle test; those workflow-specific recommendations were not evidently applicable. Capability 2’s persisted inference-schema guidance has no observed relevant implementation or reload test and is not evidently applicable to this TOML conversion task. Truncated events limit conclusions about omitted material, not the directly visible actions.

Implemented configurable Error stack serialization on branch `feature/error-stack` and committed it as `b813309`.

Verification: the build and focused stack checks passed. The regression suite passed 81 tests with the performance test excluded; in two full runs, that test failed its 700 ms limit at 1,629 ms and 2,040 ms. No test files were modified.

## Observational audit

**Outcome.** This K2 selection run loaded four capabilities, but was formally unsolved: F2P was 0/80, P2P was 80/116, and binary reward was 0. The verifier tail says displayed F2P cases were missing from its report and records `/logs/verifier/new-ctrf.json: No such file or directory`; it does not establish why those tests lacked results. Do not read 0/80 as evidence that every feature assertion executed and failed. The process ended normally with `end_turn` after a commit, not at a budget stop, although one intermediate build process segfaulted. Sources: `eval_result.json` and `trajs.json` under the supplied K2 run path; all event IDs below are `main_agent` events.

**Exploration and changes.** The student searched Error and allowed-property handling, read the transformer, public API, traversal and package configuration, and created `feature/error-stack` (events 2–13). A pre-change build succeeded, and an executable frames probe failed because its annotation was `Error` rather than `Error/frames` (14–15). The student then added option normalization, stack processing, message sanitization and a class processor registry in `/app/src/error-options.ts`, `error-stack.ts`, `error-sanitizer.ts` and `error-class-registry.ts`; it changed `/app/src/index.ts` and `transformer.ts` to expose configuration and serialize/deserialize the new representations (19–38). Subsequent compatibility edits addressed cause handling, class filtering and allowed properties (46, 60–66). Commit `b813309` contained six files, 311 insertions and 33 deletions (70–71). No test files were modified (71–72).

**Validation and costs.** Builds passed at events 40, 55, 65 and 69. A narrow frames round trip passed (42, 44); later inline checks exercised normalization, filtering order, sanitization, causes, a nested Map, off mode and a processor (62, 65). These were local checks, not official F2P. Two full local suite runs each failed the performance threshold: 1,629 ms and 2,040 ms versus 700 ms; each reported 81 passes, one failure, one skip and one todo (41–43, 56–58). The cause of the timing failures is not established. A later run excluded that test and passed the remaining 81 tests (67–69); this is not a full-suite pass. Formatting and a build retry added work: the combined formatting/build command segfaulted before its test command, but the subsequent build succeeded (47–49, 52, 55). Formatting also changed unrelated layout in `index.ts` (59), a small extra diff whose necessity is not established. The absence of committed tests limits repeatability of the inline probes.

The attempt used 34 returned tool calls, 769,918 input and 6,208 output tokens, and 914.896 seconds wall time per attempt metrics. SDK `total_cost_usd` of 4.00479 is a proxy estimate, **not an actual CLI fee**. The final student report accurately disclosed the excluded performance test (72), but its implementation claim is not formal success.

## Capability assessment

The actual loaded text is at `infer_logs/superjson-error-stack-serialization/turn_1/loaded_capabilities.md`. Direct executable behavior can be consistent with a capability without showing that the library caused it; ordinary repository inspection and testing could produce the same actions. There is no B0 run in the supplied record, so no baseline comparison or knowledge-adoption claim is available.

1. **Inspect state across transitions.** The student inspected serialization architecture and verified selected serialize/parse outputs, including nested data (4–6, 42–44, 62–65). That is consistent with examining a representation boundary. The initial intention to inspect and reproduce (1) is a claim until the later tool results; no explicit comparison of ordinary requests and continuation state is shown. Reads at 10–12 and 53–54 are truncated, limiting conclusions about what was seen.
2. **Check identity and failure feedback end to end.** A processor callback was registered and its returned output checked (62–65), but the delegation/request-identity and differentiated worker/unknown-target failure scenarios described by this capability are not visibly applicable or tested. The student’s final summary (72) is a report, not evidence of those checks.
3. **Carry input contracts into later use.** The patch normalizes configuration and consumes allowed properties; focused checks exercise a few invalid inputs and later serialization (19, 24, 62–65). This is partial boundary-contract behavior, not evidence of establishing and persisting a learned schema or testing aliases, missing and extra inputs broadly. The relevant write at 19 is truncated in the event display; the supplied final patch reveals its resulting code.
4. **Preserve meaning when changing representation.** The student inspected existing transformation code, implemented frame reconstruction and tested one stack round trip and a nested cause (4, 31–38, 42–44, 62–65). This directly matches focused representation testing in part. The probe intentionally expects trimmed whitespace, so it does not establish general semantic equivalence. No idempotence check or committed new regression tests are visible; full local regression runs failed their timing test. Read truncation prevents a complete account of the initial inspection.

## Audit outcome

This was a **B0 baseline**, with no capability library requested or loaded (`knowledge_words=0`, `actual_loaded_capabilities=null`). The observed behaviors are baseline actions, not evidence of knowledge adoption or library causation. The run ended normally with `end_turn` and a commit, not a budget or technical stop. Nevertheless, it was **formally unsolved**: official F2P passed 115/115, but P2P passed 1280/1281 and binary success was 0.

Sources: the supplied trajectory at `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-26/trajectory-to-capability-rsi-hint-rsi/outputs/trajectory_capability_20261126_020200/runs/capability_v1_test_httpx-deterministic-cookie-store_B0_r1/infer_logs/httpx-deterministic-cookie-store/turn_1/trajs.json`; official result at the same run directory’s `eval_output/httpx-deterministic-cookie-store/eval_result.json`; and the supplied final patch and verifier output. All event IDs below belong to `main_agent`.

## Exploration and changes

The student created the requested `cookie-store` branch from `main`, searched for cookie integration, and read the existing model, client, export and type definitions (events 1–6, 10–11). It checked the missing public API, receiving `AttributeError` for `httpx.CookieStore()` (events 7, 12), then inspected request and redirect paths (events 19–24). A temporary reproduction likewise failed on the missing API before implementation (events 25–26).

The executable edits added a `CookieStore` mutable mapping in `/app/httpx/_models.py`, with parsing, domain/path and secure matching, expiry, prefix checks, deterministic ordering and limits. They also added request and client integration in `/app/httpx/_models.py` and `/app/httpx/_client.py`, widened cookie types in `/app/httpx/_types.py`, and exported the class in `/app/httpx/__init__.py` (events 27–32; final patch). The later type-fix edit also added conversion from `CookieStore` to existing `Cookies` (events 49–50, 54). The final patch changed four files; event 56 records commit `745a39a`, with 305 insertions and 9 deletions. No persistent new test file appears in that patch.

Some edit and read event bodies are truncated, notably events 27, 31 and 44; the supplied final patch permits inspection of the resulting code, but not every intermediate detail. The student’s final statement that implementation and local checks passed (event 57) is a claim supported in part by tool returns, not a claim of official success.

## Validation, regression and costs

The reproduction passed after implementation, but the first local cookie/client test run failed with many failures (events 33–35). The output is truncated; one displayed failure received an unexpected HTML response. A second run after removing several proxy variables still exited unsuccessfully and included Ruff import-order errors (events 37–38). After fixing imports and also removing `NO_PROXY` variables, the targeted suite reported **317 passed, 1 skipped** (events 39–40). The sequence does not establish the cause of every earlier failure.

Mypy then reported three errors, although the compound shell command’s overall return was successful because later commands ran (events 47–48). After a further edit, mypy and Ruff passed (events 49–50). Temporary checks covered combined headers, expiry, limits, host-only and secure behavior, prefixes, conflicts, and sync/async clients; they and the reproduction passed (events 51–53). These are local checks, not the official suites. The targeted tests preceded the final type-fix edit; the reproduction and edge checks were rerun afterward, but the targeted suite was not visibly rerun.

The official verifier identified a concrete regression in `tests/test_exported_members.py::test_all_imports_are_exported`: `/app/httpx/__init__.py` placed `CookieStore` before `Cookies`, contrary to the test’s case-insensitive sorted export order. This one P2P failure explains the reported binary failure; it is not necessary to speculate about unseen failures. Official F2P passed all 115 tests, while P2P had one failure and three skips. The verifier’s process exit code 0 is not equivalent to a passing grade.

The extra reproduction, repeated regression runs, formatting, type checking and edge-case scripts incurred work beyond the implementation; they found useful issues, although the broad reruns cost time and still missed the export regression. The temporary reproduction was removed before commit (events 55–56). Metrics report 28 requested and returned tool calls, 16 model requests, 912,145 input and 6,176 output tokens, 1,723.91 seconds wall time and 1,319.437 seconds SDK time. SDK `total_cost_usd=4.715125` is a **proxy estimate**, not actual CLI billing; no actual dollar fee is established.

**Disposition.** The K2 student attempt completed normally after committing its patch; this recovery was not a new student attempt. ## Audit of K1 run

The student normally completed the run and committed `8022bb7` on branch `cookie-store` (main_agent events 51–53). This was not a budget or technical stop. Formal success was nevertheless **0**: the official evaluation passed all 115 F2P tests but 1 of 1,281 P2P tests failed. The failing test was `tests/test_exported_members.py::test_all_imports_are_exported`: `httpx/__init__.py` placed `CookieStore` before `Cookies`, contrary to the required case-insensitive export ordering. The verifier reported partial 0.9992836676 and binary reward 0. Its process exit code 0 does not mean the patch passed.

### Exploration and changes

The student created the requested branch and searched cookie types, extraction, header generation and client merging (events 1–3). It inspected `/app/httpx/_models.py`, `/app/httpx/_client.py`, `/app/httpx/_types.py` and `/app/httpx/__init__.py`, including redirect construction (events 5–13, 15–20, 22–24). A public import failed because `httpx.CookieStore` did not exist (events 9, 14); a small `/tmp/httpx_cookie_repro.py` then failed at the same point before editing (events 21, 23).

The final patch added a mutable `CookieStore` to `/app/httpx/_models.py`, with parsing, domain/path and secure matching, expiry, ordering, limits, mapping operations and conversion from existing cookie forms. It exposed the type through `/app/httpx/__init__.py` and `/app/httpx/_types.py` and integrated it into request, client merge and redirect paths in `/app/httpx/_models.py` and `/app/httpx/_client.py` (events 25–30, 42, 50; supplied `final_student_patch`). Existing `Cookies` remains the default in those visible branches, but the export-order regression shows that this did not preserve every existing behavior. The commit changed four files, with 288 insertions and nine deletions (event 52). No persistent test file was added.

### Validation, regressions and cost

After implementation, the same reproduction passed (events 29–30). Focused executable checks covered combined headers and dates, ordering and eviction, host-only and domain behavior, secure cookies, deletion, malformed attributes, prefixes, name conflicts, path boundaries, and synchronous/asynchronous client round trips; the command reported success (events 46, 48). Some of that command is truncated in the supplied event, so its complete assertions cannot be audited. Initial cookie/client regression and lint runs failed (events 31–34). Import sorting and formatting were applied, and a remaining long comment was edited (events 35, 37, 45, 47); the focused check subsequently reported lint success (event 48).

The first client-suite failure included an unexpected real HTML response; a run with proxy variables removed still failed proxy tests (events 33, 36, 38). A clean-environment rerun passed 317 tests with one skip in 117.81 seconds (events 40, 43). This supports the student's environment-qualified report in event 53, but does not establish the cause of every earlier failure. The local selection omitted the exported-members regression found by the official P2P suite. The final diff output is truncated (event 50); the separately supplied final patch permits inspection of the changes, not of any hidden execution.

The broad filesystem instruction search reached `/proc` and produced errors before a narrower `/app` search (events 2, 4, 9). Multiple suite runs and formatting consumed time; their investigation had some diagnostic value, but the record does not establish that every repeated run was necessary. The temporary reproduction was removed (event 51). Reported resources were 26 requested tool calls, all returned; 13 model requests; 833,615 input and 5,630 output tokens; and 1,289.152 seconds wall time in attempt metrics. SDK `total_cost_usd` was 4.308825, a proxy estimate, **not an actual CLI fee**; no actual dollar fee is available.

### Capability assessment

The supplied K1 `loaded_capabilities.md` contains four capabilities, and metadata says they appeared in the actual prompt and first bridge request. The following are observations consistent with their guidance, not proof of library causation: an ordinary base student could have taken the same actions. No B0 trajectory is supplied, so no baseline behavior or knowledge adoption can be assessed.

1. **Trace behavior across boundaries.** Direct actions traced request construction, client merging, redirects and response extraction, then exercised request headers and client round trips (events 15–24, 25, 46–48). The student claimed integration in event 53; the patch and checks substantiate specific integration, not a complete end-to-end audit. No explicit redirect round-trip or error-path test is visible; truncated events limit assessment of omitted assertions.
2. **Reproduce and inspect observable behavior.** The before/after reproduction and focused value assertions are direct evidence (events 21, 23, 29–30, 46–48), stronger than the student's summary claim. The initial reproduction failed at the missing API rather than reaching its cookie semantics; passing it and selected edge cases does not establish all behavior. Part of the focused command is truncated.
3. **Verify transformations beyond an example.** Cookie parsing and header production are relevant transformations, although formatter idempotence is not itself the task contract. Direct varied-input checks and the existing regression suite go beyond one example (events 31, 40, 43, 46–48). No general semantic-equivalence or repeated-transformation/idempotence check is visible; the official export failure also limits any broad quality claim. Truncation prevents a complete inventory of focused assertions.
4. **Interpret and report verification precisely.** The student reported local successes, the clean-environment qualifier and initial proxy-environment failures (event 53), consistent with observed runs. The report did not claim official F2P/P2P success; those results were produced separately. It did not detail the remaining failures in the intermediate proxy-unset run or disclose the extent of truncated output, and no pre-change baseline comparison is visible. The official regression was not known from the local checks.

**Sources:** student events and final patch supplied with this audit; trajectory `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-26/trajectory-to-capability-rsi-hint-rsi/outputs/trajectory_capability_20261126_020200/runs/capability_v1_test_httpx-deterministic-cookie-store_K1_r1/infer_logs/httpx-deterministic-cookie-store/turn_1/trajs.json`; capability file at the same `turn_1/loaded_capabilities.md`; official result `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-26/trajectory-to-capability-rsi-hint-rsi/outputs/trajectory_capability_20261126_020200/runs/capability_v1_test_httpx-deterministic-cookie-store_K1_r1/eval_output/httpx-deterministic-cookie-store/eval_result.json`.

K2’s local repairs included empty tables, comments and nested conversions (66–72, 80–88, 97–119); its sole official failure was `server .host` rather than `server.host`. K0 repaired observed intermediate syntax, proxy, empty-table and comment problems (41–98) and passed the official suites. These results support partial feature correctness for B0/K1/K2, not full compliance; successful semantic round trips did not establish the exact output assertions. K1’s promotion of an enclosing inline table was additional structural work with observable formatting effects, not demonstrated unnecessary work.

**HTTPX.** All four passed official F2P. B0 and K1 each had the same concrete P2P regression: `tests/test_exported_members.py:6` rejected `CookieStore` before `Cookies` in case-insensitive export order. This directly concerns the public requirement to leave existing behavior unchanged; the same failure without a library is contrary evidence for attributing K1’s failure to its library. K2 detected and repaired an export-order failure locally (23–28), then passed official P2P; K0 also passed it. K0 and K2 locally ran full suites reporting 1,417 passed and one skipped; B0 and K1 reported targeted clean-environment runs of 317 passed and one skipped. Earlier HTTPX suite failures and reruns were partly truncated: changes to proxy environment are consistent with environment sensitivity, but do not establish every failure’s cause. Local counts are not official F2P/P2P counts.

## Guidance, behavior and causal limits

B0 had no library. K0, K1 and K2 were recorded in both the actual prompt and first bridge request, respectively 644, 578 and 526 words. Entry into the prompt is not adoption. TOML K1’s before/after reproduction and round-trip checks (20–21, 45–50, 73–85) are consistent with its guidance, as are K2’s representation probes (21–28, 97–108). Yet B0 independently reproduced the missing API and probed representations and round trips (17–36, 47–54). HTTPX B0 similarly inspected request and redirect paths and ran focused checks (19–26, 51–53). The public tasks themselves called for much of this work. No cited student statement establishes reliance on a library.

K2 is not simply identical wording: its representation rule specifically says an equivalence comparison must reflect meaningful units and must not disable safety for unrelated categories; K1 separately asks for semantic preservation, idempotence, safety validation and mixed-form checks, without that explicit scoping constraint. K2 also explicitly distinguishes continuation state from new input. These are substantive differences in transferable emphasis, but overlap is substantial; neither is shown to have caused a Test outcome. Different delivered lengths and content, despite shared sources and budgets, confound an interpretation as organization alone. No source ablation supports a marginal ranking of individual source trajectories’ learning value.

## Work and resource costs

Numbers below are requested tools / model requests; input tokens, including the cached subset / output tokens; wall / SDK seconds. All requested tools returned. Token figures are actual CLI input accounting: **do not add cached input again**.

| Task | Group | Tools / requests | Input incl. cached / output | Wall / SDK s |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| TOML | B0 | 47 / 30 | 2,117,232 (535,296 cached) / 8,496 | 1,067 / 785 |
| TOML | K0 | 51 / 33 | 2,235,018 (445,440) / 9,702 | 1,118 / 835 |
| TOML | K1 | 47 / 35 | 2,128,874 (212,480) / 9,339 | 1,122 / 823 |
| TOML | K2 | 61 / 34 | 2,315,718 (549,632) / 9,295 | 1,089 / 801 |
| HTTPX | B0 | 28 / 16 | 912,145 (223,616) / 6,176 | 1,724 / 1,319 |
| HTTPX | K0 | 42 / 17 | 985,997 (208,128) / 6,540 | 1,859 / 1,439 |
| HTTPX | K1 | 26 / 13 | 833,615 (262,656) / 5,630 | 1,289 / 903 |
| HTTPX | K2 | 24 / 17 | 1,047,020 (306,432) / 5,872 | 1,654 / 1,241 |

SDK dollar estimates for TOML B0/K0/K1/K2 were approximately $10.80/$11.42/$10.88/$11.81; HTTPX estimates were $4.72/$5.09/$4.31/$5.38. They are proxies, not settled CLI billing; some SDK and attempt cache fields disagree. Repeated suites and probes incurred cost but often exposed defects. Clearer redundant work includes HTTPX K2’s second pre-edit missing-symbol diagnosis (7–12, 17–18), and K1’s broad search into `/proc` before narrowing it (2, 4, 9). Neither establishes a general library-induced waste effect.

## Selection and recovery

The supplied Selection evidence is limited to the SuperJSON K2 recovery; the original full Selection public requirements and individual Selection audits are not present here. Consequently, their substantive task compliance and all candidate-specific retention decisions cannot be re-audited from this record. Apply the saved rule without inventing grounds to drop: **retain any otherwise inconclusive candidate unchanged**, unless leakage, absent injection, invalid format, or regression with clear causal evidence is actually established. The supplied recovery alone establishes none of those drop grounds.

The original Selection K2 result recorded 0/80 F2P and 80/116 P2P with a missing `new-ctrf.json`; missing reported cases are not demonstrated assertion failures. Preserve that original record. The one actual same-patch diagnostic, at `R/runs/capability_eval_diagnostic_selection_K2_02/eval_output/superjson-error-stack-serialization/eval_result.json`, independently reported 80/80 and 116/116. Invocation 01 did not run the evaluator. The 13,143-byte patch was unchanged; no student retry or test/environment change occurred. The missing report’s cause remains unknown. Initial student wall time was 914.896 seconds; recovered end-to-end time was 1,476.782 seconds, including triage, with 89.220 seconds diagnostic evaluation—not an additional student attempt. Test libraries were frozen beforehand; no retrospective Test selection or tuning is warranted.

## Conclusions

**Confirmed:** K0 passed both Test cells; K2 passed HTTPX but not TOML; B0 and K1 were formally unsolved in both, despite substantial partial correctness. Official retained-functionality results were complete except for the identified B0/K1 HTTPX export regression. Matching guidance and executable behavior occurred, but baseline behavior also matched several themes.

**Unresolved hypotheses:** Whether any library changed behavior or outcomes, whether the K2-specific constraints helped, and why the original Selection report was missing remain unproven.

**Specific limitations:** One stochastic attempt per cell, different library texts and lengths, finite and partly skipped tests, truncated trajectory outputs, inconsistent cache accounting, no source ablation, and missing full Selection requirements/audits prevent causal ranking or comprehensive Selection reassessment.

# 从历史轨迹提取可迁移能力：最终研究汇报

**主 Test 的实际结果并不支持“轨迹知识一定优于基线”这一预设。**在两道独立 Test 任务、每组每题一次的正式评价中，K0 两题均成功，K2 一题成功，B0 和 K1 均未取得完整成功；各组仍有不同程度的局部正确性。尤其是 K2 在 TOML 任务仅差一项 F2P，但正式成功仍为零；HTTPX 的 B0 和 K1 全部 F2P 通过，却各有一项 P2P 回归。这个样本只有每组两题，不能据此断言显著性、稳定排序或知识的因果收益。

主 Selection 与 Test 的计划单元已有结果，以下称为**核心结果闭合**；这不等于六小时监测窗口、可选工作和清理核算已经结束。本报告仅呈现已供给的完成证据，不修改实验。最终监测、资源清理及完整账目以文末追加材料为准。

## A. 历史证据审计：覆盖、关键失败与教师链

### 覆盖边界

历史清单共索引 **257 条文件记录**：学生 117、教师 104、其他历史预检轨迹 36。它是文件清单，不是 257 次独立尝试，也绝不是 257 个文件均已深审。学生中深审 10 个文件、共 913 个事件；其中进入开发知识池的 D01—D08 是 8 条完整序列、397 个事件。另有冻结后只用于补充审计的 E01、E02，共 516 个事件：245 和 271 个事件 ID 均纳入，但长字符串截至 1,800 字符；它们未输入知识生成或学生。教师文件中深审 4 个完整文件、49 个事件；另有 107 个学生文件和 100 个教师文件未深审。历史预检文件也不能因被索引而视为逐事件审计。出版目录 `hintrsi` 是别名或副本，不是新尝试。

首次逐案审计包没有提供完整历史原始任务描述，因而当时只能依据轨迹、实际提示和评价重建目标；成功完成的[教师链补充审计](file:///srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-26/trajectory-to-capability-rsi-hint-rsi/outputs/trajectory_capability_20261126_020200/audit/audit_teacher_chain_reduced.md)后来补入了任务描述，澄清了委派、Igel 和 SQLfmt 的要求。不能把后补材料说成首次逐案审计已经看到，也不能把后来完整审计中可见的失败细节反向归入当时的知识输入。

### 必审代码案例

- **Claude 委派 B/H/M/I。**D01/B1 调用了要求遇到非 Anthropic 标记时停下询问的 skill，检查到其他提供者后请求澄清，空补丁；这是有行为证据的指令遵循，不是已尝试算法的失败。D02/H1 的实际系统提示含参考指导；事件 30—33 的模拟续接复现先失败，34—53 修改接口、处理器和适配器，59—61 同一复现通过，但正式 F2P 6/7、P2P 31/31，空文本子代理场景未通过，完整原因未确定。生成文件缺失导致类型检查受阻，测试、清理和提交未完成。D03/M2 声称受只读权限约束并空补丁，但没有可见工具拒绝，不能把其自述当作已证实的权限故障。D04/I1 因 skill 的提供者歧义停下询问，未实现或测试，正式 0/7、31/31；已有参考提示不等于实现被采纳。
- **Claude I2 的失败—诊断—修复链。**D05 事件 27—28 首先复现委派链未续接。第一次在线教师检查要求查看已有上下文与新指令或图像的真实请求；事件 49—51 的探针显示新输入被丢弃，52—57 修改续接条件，95—97 再检查普通请求和续接消息。98—100 又修改保存的图像上下文，但展示的探针没有单独覆盖这最后一次修改。第二次教师检查要求比较成功、工作者失败和未知目标的反馈与调用 ID；事件 84—85 的模拟检查确实比较了结果、错误标志和 ID。最终三文件提交，正式 7/7、31/31；与此同时，本地 handler 测试仍有失败，学生在该环境的基线上也观察到同一失败，另一个提供者套件无法转换。正式通过不能抹去这些局限，时序一致也不是随机对照因果证明。
- **Igel B3。**D06 事件 25—26 的复现显示选择特征未生效，后续实现原始 schema 的保存、加载、别名和错误传播。根目录测试失败，从预期测试目录运行则两项通过；正式 23/24、2/2，奖励 0。完整审计可见失败是描述中保存的 `feature_schema.joblib` 路径被测试直接加载时找不到，而补丁自身按描述文件目录解析相对路径；这是该记录支持的具体路径契约不一致，不应冒充当初截断抽取包中已知的教训。D07/H1 则因要求的 `main` 不可用而询问，空补丁；D06 选择 `master` 并披露。补充任务描述确认确有从 `main` 建分支并提交的要求，但不能据此推断 D07 若继续就会成功。
- **SQLfmt source 13。**D08 事件 18—21 发现 CREATE TABLE 被当作不透明 DATA，52—57 遇到并处理基于物理行的安全等价检查不匹配，随后检查样例和幂等，事件 78—79 的聚焦套件通过。正式却为 F2P 30/32、P2P 1271/1273，奖励 0；完整审计中一个可见格式差异为 `in (` 与期望 `in(`，其他截断失败不能臆断。局部修复和大量本地通过不等于完整语义或回归覆盖。

教师链显示，最初教师读参考 diff、handler、适配器和测试后形成完整 Hint，再压缩为实际注入的参考；H1 复核指出续接已出现但验证不足，I1 复核提出处理 skill 歧义，I2 初始提示增加“不必因此替换其他提供者”的提醒，之后两次在线检查对应了上面的实际探针。教师的参考比较不是对正式失败根因的证明；提示中要求不归因于参考，也不能作为学生独立发明的证据。

历史 Ofox 使用的是 `deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017`，10 次模型尝试为 3 成功、3 失败、4 不完整，另有 2 次模型前基础设施启动；不能与新 Terra 学生作控制比较。历史 batch 12 的新段 53 个已评分中 1 成功、52 正式未解，另有 3 中断和 3 个任务未开始；停止原因是意外原生操作 `mcp_tool_call`，不能把全部结果归因于算法缺陷。

## B. 原工程复用、真实条件与工程修复

实验基于原始 `source_parallel_13`，公开提交为 `c0132d7e381ff660354d7a4403e29ee6107354f9`；37 个比对文件与公开检出逐内容一致，未做下载或哈希验证。结果目录是增量副本：沿用原 SDK、Bridge、评价器、验证过的 VM、外层容器和防火墙隔离，而非另造学生或评分器。原 SDK 内层 `bwrap`/`socat` 可用性限制仍在，不能声称已解决。

实际修改集中在能力文件路径的编排转发、SDK 系统提示追加，以及评价日志保存：`run_cc_sdk.py` 的小修复让 B0 走已有 preset+append 路径并获得**空 reminder**，不向 B0 添加知识，非空知识路径代码保持不变；编排层把 `capability_path` 从误放的 `step_get_hint` 移到真正的 `step_solve`；`eval_deep_swe.py` 仅在容器命令**结束后**另存完整 stdout/stderr，不改评分、测试、命令或环境。元数据投影和清单统计也修正了字段读取：正式 F2P/P2P 原来在顶层，第一次抽取投影只保留 reward、exit、stderr，修复后两组知识重新生成。未手工修补任何学生解答。

全局默认原为不同的 `gpt-6.1-sol/xhigh`，但实际 Bridge 忽略用户配置并显式指定 **`gpt-6.1-terra/low`**。真实入口、服务、Selection/Test 队列和完整 CLI 参数见[实际命令记录](file:///srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-26/trajectory-to-capability-rsi-hint-rsi/outputs/trajectory_capability_20261126_020200/commands_used.md)。其基础形式是 `codex exec --ephemeral --json --ignore-user-config --sandbox read-only --model gpt-6.1-terra -c 'model_reasoning_effort="low"'`，并禁用原生 shell、浏览器、插件、原生 skill 等；原 SDK 消息和工具被序列化到新的 CLI 请求，不能宣称与原生 API 的角色和采样设置完全等价。学生每次预算 1,800 秒、8 CPU、128 GiB，单轮；温度等沿 CLI 默认。

**生产转发故障及两次统一复核。**中性 SDK fixture 证明了下游追加机制，却没有覆盖完整编排适配器。真实 Selection K0 初始化时发现 `capability_path` 未到达 `solve_r1`：旧 B0 已正式成功，K0 在任何模型请求前中止；两条均保留，不计入当前核心比较。修复转发后，四组按统一软件重跑。审计教师包也曾以 1,153,690 字符超过 1,048,576 上限，在模型响应前失败；随后仅省去 D05 已完整审计的重复在线事件上下文，四条教师轨迹仍在精简包中，成功完成教师链补充审计。失败请求无用量回报，不能计作零成本的正常回答。

随后实际请求显示，SDK 空追加与非空追加路径的身份句不同：旧 B0 为“a Claude agent”，知识组为“Claude Code … running within the Claude Agent SDK”。因此旧 `capability_v1` 四组 Selection 及对应审计、分数均保留为**被取代的输入条件证据**；四组按预存顺序再次以 `capability_v1_matched_prompt` 复核，而不是只重跑某个成绩。最早启动的 TOML K1 和 HTTPX K2 用的仍是未改动的非空路径，予以保留。实际首请求逐文本比较表明，三个任务各组在精确移除知识文本后，公共系统文本、工具定义和非系统消息均与 B0 相同；见[条件核验](file:///srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-26/trajectory-to-capability-rsi-hint-rsi/outputs/trajectory_capability_20261126_020200/results/model_condition_validation.json)。中性 fixture 的计费头版本后缀与历史生产不同，故不宣称 fixture 全字节相同；实际主组比较包含生产计费头。匹配首请求不代表随机生成轨迹相同。

**K2 Selection 评价异常。**原结果保留奖励 0、F2P 0/80、P2P 80/116，但 `new-ctrf.json` 缺失，报告没有完整列出测试，不能说 80 项断言执行后失败。首次诊断启动器因归档后找不到顶层补丁而未运行评价，约 0.206 秒；随后仅一次实际诊断以直接内容相同的 13,143 字节补丁、相同环境重新评价，首份完整报告为 80/80、116/116，奖励 1。不是多次试验择优，没有学生重试、代码或知识改进。原始输出仅留 8,000 字符尾部，根因未知，Node/JIT 并非已证实原因。诊断评价约 89.220 秒；恢复后的 1,476.782 秒墙钟包含排查和恢复，不是技能效率效应，也不能再把诊断时间重复相加。[异常及恢复审计](file:///srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-26/trajectory-to-capability-rsi-hint-rsi/outputs/trajectory_capability_20261126_020200/audit/evaluation_diagnostic_selection_K2.md)与原始结果均保留。

## C. 知识构造、对照与冻结

B0 不加载能力；K0 只用开发任务描述和教师自身一般先验，不读取学生轨迹、实现或测试；K1 对相同原始轨迹按时间线蒸馏；K2 先区分**推断子目标**与**实际观察状态**，再按功能目标或测试类别对齐，最后生成库。K2 没有额外 GT、隐藏测试或额外学生尝试。

K1/K2 均使用 D01—D08 的同一机械过滤输入、相同 615,929 字符原始来源、相同模型与每组两次生成调用；单次上限在看到分数前设为 700,000 字符。逐字符串、工具输入和补丁均有固定截断，因此并非每个源文件的所有细节都进入模型。元数据修复前 K1/K2 各两次调用及原始输出保留为额外成本，修复后各再两次；不是根据 Selection 或 Test 分数重写。统一交付规则在任何 Selection 分数及知识组尝试前确定：保留生成顺序中的前四个完整能力单元，不改写。最终 K0/K1/K2 分别为 **644/578/526 词**；K2 原始候选 810 词被截为 526，因此没有更长 K2 的交付优势，但内容和长度仍不相等，不能把差异解释为纯粹的表格组织效应。

每个条件只有一个 V1 候选。预定规则仅在泄露答案、未注入、格式无效或有明确因果证据的退化时淘汰；库审查未发现泄露或格式问题，旧 Selection 的单次差异不足以证明由库导致退化，故均保留。知识在较早 Selection 后、任何 Test 前于 19:37:13 UTC 冻结；后来的匹配复核和 Test 反馈均未更新它们。没有 V2、递归更新或权重训练。所有原始候选、修复前版本、中间分析和冻结副本保留。

## D. 正式结果、额外启动与成本

正式成功是评价器的完整二元标准；F2P 是新需求测试的辅助指标，P2P 是所测已有行为保持情况，二者都不等于全部可能行为。缺报告和模型前技术中止不应作为普通算法失败。Selection 是开发选择证据，Test 是冻结后的独立任务结果，不能合并成同一成功率。

<<EXTRA_RESULTS_TABLE>>

匹配 Selection 中 B0、K1 和恢复评价后的 K2 正式通过，K0 的一个 `classFilter` 与 cause 消毒交互未通过；旧 Selection 与新复核结果不同本身提醒我们，单次生成波动和输入修复都会影响观察。Test 的两题每组仅一次：K0 为 2/2，K2 为 1/2，B0 与 K1 为 0/2。这些描述不构成显著性检验，也不证明 K0 或 K2 的知识导致结果。HTTPX 每组 P2P 另有三项跳过，有限通过并非完整兼容性证明。

核心表逐行给出真实工具请求及返回、模型请求、输入、输出、缓存子集和墙钟／SDK 时间；缓存已包含在输入内，不可再相加。例如 TOML K2 为 61 次工具返回、34 次模型请求、2,315,718 输入、9,295 输出、其中 549,632 缓存输入，墙钟 1,088.810 秒；HTTPX K2 为 24 次工具返回、17 次模型请求、1,047,020 输入、5,872 输出、其中 306,432 缓存输入，墙钟 1,653.912 秒。它们是实际单次成本，不是稳定效率差。各评估诊断是仅评价成本，首次无补丁启动甚至未执行评价；两者均不是新学生尝试。

知识生成成本也不能忽略：修复前 K1 和 K2 各两次调用，分别记录输入 188,824 和 189,425 token；修复后各两次，分别 189,020 和 189,788。K0 两次输入 7,320。上述均有输出和各自缓存子集；完整分类账见索引。SDK 报告美元是代理估计，真实结算 CLI 美元未知，不能与 CLI token 账重复相加。部分 SDK 与尝试指标的缓存字段不一致，应保留各自口径而非强行调和。

### 条件性 Hint 探索

<<OPTIONAL_HINT_RESULTS>>

该探索若有结果，也只是开发任务上的即时观察：各变体从相同初始代码、独立新会话开始，并非恢复到共同中间状态的严格反事实重放；没有独立 Hint 迁移测试，不应声称 Hint 迁移收益。主 Test 冻结库不从该探索更新。

## E. 行为、采纳、修复与迁移边界

**先证明输入，再看行为，再限制归因。**实际首请求和 `loaded_capabilities.md` 证明 K0/K1/K2 的文本进入学生请求；它们不证明学生依赖该文本。匹配 Selection 的 K1 在事件 13—15 先做失败复现，27—29 检查边界往返；K2 在 42—44、62—65 检查序列化、反序列化和嵌套 Map。这与各自规则一致，但 B0 的事件 19—22 也在无库条件下做了失败 frames 复现。Test 中 TOML B0 检查了点分键及往返，HTTPX B0 检查请求和重定向路径；因此“观察到检查”不能自动升级为“知识造成检查”。历史 D05 两次在线教师指令后紧接的针对性探针，是较强的同次采纳证据，但仍无隔离教师效应的对照。

K2 不只是把 K1 排成更漂亮的表。K2 明确提出安全等价比较应针对**有意义的表示单元**，物理布局可能过严或过松，而且不能为一类表示关闭其他类别的安全检查；K1 有语义保持、幂等和安全验证，但没有同样明确的比较粒度与范围限定。K2 还明确区分新输入和续接状态。这是实质性的可迁移限定，不等于全新研究概念，也未证明本次 Test 因此成功。两库都覆盖边界追踪、下游输入和转换验证，文字、长度与内容差异共同混杂。

修复与失败应按真实轨迹解释。TOML K2 在事件 66—72、80—88、97—119 修正空表、注释和嵌套转换等中间问题，却仍在正式测试输出 `server .host`，语义往返不能代替精确格式契约。K0 同样经历局部语法和注释修复后通过两套正式测试；这不是证明它的库必然更好。HTTPX K2 事件 23—28 本地发现并修正导出顺序，正式通过；B0 和 K1 的同一导出顺序 P2P 失败，恰好反对把 K1 失败简单归因于其知识。若测试输出只给出部分尾部，不应发明隐藏测试诊断。

开销也有正反两面：重复套件和定制探针消耗时间，却常发现实际问题；HTTPX K2 重复确认缺失符号、K1 的宽泛搜索进入 `/proc` 是可观察的额外工作，但没有证据说明它们由库造成。Selection 多组本地性能阈值失败，没有可比的修改前计时，不能宣称补丁导致性能回归。没有源轨迹消融，混合池也不支持给 D01—D08 各自的学习价值或边际迁移贡献排名。

## F. Scene 证据链与可迁移方案

Scene 的证据范围不同于代码实验：初始审计 136 个唯一文本文件，补充四个完整文本后共 **140 个，132 个全文、8 个仅前缀**；另有两个旧二进制 checkpoint 只读探测。六个原始轨迹 JSONL 均只审前缀，另审 25 个完整阶段事件日志、21 个增量补丁、10 个构建文件；三个有限视觉案例涉及六张渲染图和两张不同参考照片。T01 与 E02 的参考是同一历史厨房，不能当作两个独立场景。27 个 bundle 仅索引，未深审内容；输出和公开归档可能是复制件，文件数不是独立尝试数。

**识别—诊断—更新—采纳链。**历史 D01 第 4 阶段，教师指出显示器背板与浅色背景难以区分，希望改变对比和方向并让支架坐在桌面，同时承认无法区分洗白与遮挡。实际视觉修订补丁修改背板材质并旋转面板和边框；阶段记录和保存状态支持这些操作确实发生。教师随后报告面板更清楚但支撑仍难辨，状态只是 `advance_with_issue`，不是质量验收。第 5 阶段相机及天花板调整后，教师又报告椅子裁切、植物遮住暖气等新问题；一次修订可改善局部而带来其他退化。

[SG01 只读几何补充](file:///srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-26/trajectory-to-capability-rsi-hint-rsi/outputs/trajectory_capability_20261126_020200/audit/audit_SG01.md)用原 Blender 4.2.10、单线程、无 GPU、无渲染加载两个已有保存状态，不保存原文件。每个状态记录 874 个对象，选取 48 个语义相关网格及 1,128 对 AABB 下界。面板材质与包围盒改变，支架直立件和底座包围盒不变，相机也不变；这支持执行事实，不证明桌面接触、物体连接或视觉质量。正的 AABB 距离下界只说明该对包围盒分离；零下界既不证明接触也不证明正确。不同部件分离或不同建模实现也不自动是错误。

其他历史链中，H04 在既定 Selection 规则下被保留，后续两个学生构建实际执行了地标投影及相机试探；数值投影支持特定点的屏幕位置，不证明可见轮廓或照片匹配。M07 的只读材质诊断被执行和复用，H08 则按既定规则被拒绝；诊断工具复用不是学生质量改善。M0/M1 的厨房记录有不同既往提示和结果，不能将最终图差异归因于 M1。尤其，相机位置或焦距变化可以合法改变投影大小，而几何尺寸完全不变；不能把未缩放几何误称为实现错误。

**可行的迁移表达，而非已完成试验：**把程序行为映射为三维语义状态及其前后变化；把行为约束映射为几何、支撑、遮挡和对象关系；把单元测试映射为几何检查与渲染检查的组合；把跨任务对齐改为跨对象、跨场景功能对齐。每条规则应区分图像观察、三维诊断假设、实际补丁和独立验证，保留相机—几何—材质—光照的混杂。这里没有实施新的 Scene 重建、学习、质量迁移试验或审美教师；代码任务成绩不是这些库能改善 Scene 的证据。

## G. 文献重叠与贡献边界

本次实际打开的是以下论文**摘要页**，并非全文系统综述。多轨迹归纳和可复用技能已有 [Trace2Skill](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.25158)；学生失败与教师轨迹对照、用重跑验证技能已有 [SKILL-KD](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.28048)，修复与退化的实证评估已有 [SkillGen](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.10999)。因此，多轨迹总结和技能验证都不是本工作的首创。

教师指导与新会话练习复用见 [Socratic Skill Learning](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.17860)，面向学生的诊断及匹配开发集准入见 [Teaching the Harness](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.13144)。本例 D05 的具体贡献只是可追溯地显示提示后的请求检查和反馈检查，不是证明教师指导本身新颖。调试假说需要有针对性的干预、且同一失败可能有不同修复，与 [DoVer](https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.06749) 的摘要范围重叠；本报告没有把事后相似性当作干预验证。自然语言反思和测试更新也与 [GEPA](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.19457) 重叠。

在三维方面，[SceneEvolve](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.37046) 摘要涉及固定模型、动作和后端下的可执行 3D 代码及教师驱动 harness 演化；[SimWorld Studio](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.09423) 摘要涉及验证反馈支持的 3D 环境代码工具、技能与课程演化。冻结模型自我改进、教师引导或 harness 验证均不应宣称为新颖。最审慎的定位是：本研究在极小、单次的条件下，为**显式状态对齐、尽量独立于实现的知识表述**提供了有限探索性证据；K2 有可指出的实质限定，但其独立效果、效率和 Scene 迁移均未被证明。

# 从历史轨迹提取可迁移能力：最终研究汇报

**主 Test 的实际结果并不支持“轨迹知识一定优于基线”这一预设。**在两道独立 Test 任务、每组每题一次的正式评价中，K0 两题均成功，K2 一题成功，B0 和 K1 均未取得完整成功；各组仍有不同程度的局部正确性。尤其是 K2 在 TOML 任务仅差一项 F2P，但正式成功仍为零；HTTPX 的 B0 和 K1 全部 F2P 通过，却各有一项 P2P 回归。这个样本只有每组两题，不能据此断言显著性、稳定排序或知识的因果收益。这里的独立性限于可访问的已记录历史，详见 C 节。

主 Selection 与 Test 的计划单元已有结果，以下称为**核心结果闭合**；这不等于六小时监测窗口、可选工作和清理核算已经结束。本报告仅呈现已供给的完成证据，不修改实验。最终监测、资源清理及完整账目以文末追加材料为准。

## A. 历史证据审计：覆盖、关键失败与教师链

### 覆盖边界

**先证明输入，再看行为，再限制归因。**实际首请求和 `loaded_capabilities.md` 证明 K0/K1/K2 的文本进入学生请求；它们不证明学生依赖该文本。匹配 Selection 的 K1 在事件 13—15 先做失败复现，27—29 检查边界往返；K2 在 42—44、62—65 检查序列化、反序列化和嵌套 Map。这与各自规则一致，但 B0 的事件 19—22 也在无库条件下做了失败 frames 复现。Test 中 TOML B0 检查了点分键及往返，HTTPX B0 检查请求和重定向路径；因此“观察到检查”不能自动升级为“知识造成检查”。历史 D05 两次在线教师指令后紧接的针对性探针，是较强的同次采纳证据，但仍无隔离教师效应的对照。

K2 不只是把 K1 排成更漂亮的表。K2 明确提出安全等价比较应针对**有意义的表示单元**，物理布局可能过严或过松，而且不能为一类表示关闭其他类别的安全检查；K1 有语义保持、幂等和安全验证，但没有同样明确的比较粒度与范围限定。K2 还明确区分新输入和续接状态。这是实质性的可迁移限定，不等于全新研究概念，也未证明本次 Test 因此成功。两库都覆盖边界追踪、下游输入和转换验证，文字、长度与内容差异共同混杂。

修复与失败应按真实轨迹解释。TOML K2 在事件 66—72、80—88、97—119 修正空表、注释和嵌套转换等中间问题，却仍在正式测试输出 `server .host`，语义往返不能代替精确格式契约。K0 同样经历局部语法和注释修复后通过两套正式测试；这不是证明它的库必然更好。HTTPX K2 事件 23—28 本地发现并修正导出顺序，正式通过；B0 和 K1 的同一导出顺序 P2P 失败，恰好反对把 K1 失败简单归因于其知识。若测试输出只给出部分尾部，不应发明隐藏测试诊断。

开销也有正反两面：重复套件和定制探针消耗时间，却常发现实际问题；HTTPX K2 重复确认缺失符号、K1 的宽泛搜索进入 `/proc` 是可观察的额外工作，但没有证据说明它们由库造成。Selection 多组本地性能阈值失败，没有可比的修改前计时，不能宣称补丁导致性能回归。没有源轨迹消融，混合池也不支持给 D01—D08 各自的学习价值或边际迁移贡献排名。

## F. Scene 证据链与可迁移方案

最新本地审计的 stagewise 分支为 `d29db8ddb223dfe2899fb7a158c7fcbb1bfda690`，与可获得的公开 stagewise 相同；它领先且不同于公开 main `355930a79d1d7ceecaddd8b549fa7a88121e97bd`。

Scene 的证据范围不同于代码实验：初始审计 136 个唯一文本文件，补充四个完整文本后共 **140 个，132 个全文、8 个仅前缀**；另有两个旧二进制 checkpoint 只读探测。六个原始轨迹 JSONL 均只审前缀，另审 25 个完整阶段事件日志、21 个增量补丁、10 个构建文件；三个有限视觉案例涉及六张渲染图和两张不同参考照片。T01 与 E02 的参考是同一历史厨房，不能当作两个独立场景。27 个 bundle 仅索引，未深审内容；输出和公开归档可能是复制件，文件数不是独立尝试数。

**识别—诊断—更新—采纳链。**历史 D01 第 4 阶段，教师指出显示器背板与浅色背景难以区分，希望改变对比和方向并让支架坐在桌面，同时承认无法区分洗白与遮挡。实际视觉修订补丁修改背板材质并旋转面板和边框；阶段记录和保存状态支持这些操作确实发生。教师随后报告面板更清楚但支撑仍难辨，状态只是 `advance_with_issue`，不是质量验收。第 5 阶段相机及天花板调整后，教师又报告椅子裁切、植物遮住暖气等新问题；一次修订可改善局部而带来其他退化。

[SG01 只读几何补充](/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-26/trajectory-to-capability-rsi-hint-rsi/outputs/trajectory_capability_20261126_020200/audit/audit_SG01.md)用原 Blender 4.2.10、单线程、无 GPU、无渲染加载两个已有保存状态，不保存原文件。每个状态记录 874 个对象，选取 48 个语义相关网格及 1,128 对 AABB 下界。面板材质与包围盒改变，支架直立件和底座包围盒不变，相机也不变；这支持执行事实，不证明桌面接触、物体连接或视觉质量。正的 AABB 距离下界只说明该对包围盒分离；零下界既不证明接触也不证明正确。不同部件分离或不同建模实现也不自动是错误。

其他历史链中，H04 在既定 Selection 规则下被保留，后续两个学生构建实际执行了地标投影及相机试探；数值投影支持特定点的屏幕位置，不证明可见轮廓或照片匹配。M07 的只读材质诊断被执行和复用，H08 则按既定规则被拒绝；诊断工具复用不是学生质量改善。M0/M1 的厨房记录有不同既往提示和结果，不能将最终图差异归因于 M1。尤其，相机位置或焦距变化可以合法改变投影大小，而几何尺寸完全不变；不能把未缩放几何误称为实现错误。

**可行的迁移表达，而非已完成试验：**把程序行为映射为三维语义状态及其前后变化；把行为约束映射为几何、支撑、遮挡和对象关系；把单元测试映射为几何检查与渲染检查的组合；把跨任务对齐改为跨对象、跨场景功能对齐。每条规则应区分图像观察、三维诊断假设、实际补丁和独立验证，保留相机—几何—材质—光照的混杂。这里没有实施新的 Scene 重建、学习、质量迁移试验或审美教师；代码任务成绩不是这些库能改善 Scene 的证据。

## G. 文献重叠与贡献边界

本次实际打开的是以下论文**摘要页**，并非全文系统综述。多轨迹归纳和可复用技能已有 [Trace2Skill](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.25158)；学生失败与教师轨迹对照、用重跑验证技能已有 [SKILL-KD](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.28048)，修复与退化的实证评估已有 [SkillGen](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.10999)。因此，多轨迹总结和技能验证都不是本工作的首创。

教师指导与新会话练习复用见 [Socratic Skill Learning](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.17860)，面向学生的诊断及匹配开发集准入见 [Teaching the Harness](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.13144)。本例 D05 的具体贡献只是可追溯地显示提示后的请求检查和反馈检查，不是证明教师指导本身新颖。调试假说需要有针对性的干预、且同一失败可能有不同修复，与 [DoVer](https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.06749) 的摘要范围重叠；本报告没有把事后相似性当作干预验证。自然语言反思和测试更新也与 [GEPA](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.19457) 重叠。

在三维方面，[SceneEvolve](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.37046) 摘要涉及固定模型、动作和后端下的可执行 3D 代码及教师驱动 harness 演化；[SimWorld Studio](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.09423) 摘要涉及验证反馈支持的 3D 环境代码工具、技能与课程演化。冻结模型自我改进、教师引导或 harness 验证均不应宣称为新颖。最审慎的定位是：本研究在极小、单次的条件下，为**显式状态对齐、尽量独立于实现的知识表述**提供了有限探索性证据；K2 有可指出的实质限定，但其独立效果、效率和 Scene 迁移均未被证明。

Verification: the frontend and backend builds and backend type-check passed. The delegation reproduction passed. The existing handler suite had one failure in abort-controller cleanup; the same failure was reproduced on `main` before the changes.

## Observations

This is an optional Development Hint trial, not a fresh transfer test. The supplied evidence covers **one NoHint attempt only**; it contains no Error, Strategy, or Exploration feedback to inspect or compare. NoHint had no online teacher: SDK callbacks, server teacher checks, teacher model requests, and delivered Hints were all zero, and `teacher_checks` is empty. Thus there was no candidate or screening call, screened or delivered Hint, or subsequent Hint-entry/action adoption to assess. These are distinct stages; a model call alone would not establish delivery.

The task was recursive delegation in the multi-agent chat flow. In the recorded trajectory, `main_agent` created a branch from `main` (events 1–2), inspected the handler, providers, and tests (events 3–26), then wrote a local mock-provider reproduction. **Before the change**, it failed because the child was not invoked (events 27–30). The student added a tool-use ID to `/app/backend/providers/types.ts` and `/app/backend/providers/claude-code.ts`, and changed `/app/backend/handlers/multiAgentChat.ts` to run delegated agents recursively, collect text or errors, detect cycles and unknown targets, and re-invoke the parent with a JSON tool result (events 31–44; final patch). **After the change**, the same reproduction reported “Delegation works” (events 52–54 and 69–70). This executable before/after evidence supports that narrow mock scenario, not the complete contract.

Local validation was mixed. A typecheck initially failed because the generated `cli/version.ts` was missing; after generation it passed. A backend build initially lacked the frontend build, but the subsequent frontend and backend builds passed (events 49–54, 59–61). The handler test command failed after correction of an invocation error; the student also ran it against the original handler and observed failure (events 56–67). The supplied test output is truncated, so the final claim that both failures were the same abort-controller cleanup failure is not independently established by the displayed output. After a further delegated-error change, typecheck and the reproduction passed again, while the handler suite failed (events 75–81). The reproduction was removed, the diff minimized, typecheck and bundling passed, and commit `271e981` was created (events 83–86). These local checks are not the hidden formal tests.

**Official outcome:** the verifier applied an 8,635-byte patch and wrote base backend and frontend JUnit reports, but evaluation timed out with exit code 137. The supplied record has no completed F2P or P2P counts, no observed verifier reward, and no formal success result. Neither an algorithmic failure nor full success can be inferred from that timeout; its root cause is unknown and there was no same-patch retry. Implemented recursive delegation and committed it on branch `recursive-agent-delegation` as `717142e`.

The handler runs delegated agents, feeds their textual results back to the delegating agent, and handles unknown agents, failures, and circular delegation. The Anthropic provider now declares and parses the delegation tool.

**Verification:** The frontend and backend builds, backend type-check, and delegation reproduction passed. # Post-hoc audit: Error Development Hint

## Scope and evidence

This was an optional **hint-exploration** trial, not a fresh transfer test. The supplied record covers one Error run; it does not provide comparable Strategy or Exploration trajectories or outcomes. Attempts started from common initial code in fresh contexts, not a restored shared intermediate state. Their stochastic trajectories are therefore not strict counterfactual replays. NoHint had no online teacher.

Source references below use these exact paths:

- **Trajectory:** `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-26/trajectory-to-capability-rsi-hint-rsi/outputs/trajectory_capability_20261126_020200/runs/capability_hint_development_claude-code-by-agents-recursive-delegation_Error_r1/infer_logs/claude-code-by-agents-recursive-delegation/turn_1/trajs.json`

- **Evaluation:** `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-26/trajectory-to-capability-rsi-hint-rsi/outputs/trajectory_capability_20261126_020200/runs/capability_hint_development_claude-code-by-agents-recursive-delegation_Error_r1/eval_output/claude-code-by-agents-recursive-delegation/eval_result.json`

## Observations

**Initial state and intervention.** The first Error request was available and recorded as equal to NoHint in system messages, non-system messages, and tool definitions, with no persistent capability marker. Guided arms deliberately had empty initial Hint files; that does not contradict a later online delivery.

There were **two SDK teacher callbacks**, but only **one server teacher check**. At check 1, tool count 20, a candidate model identified a provider/handler compatibility gap, and a separate screen model approved delivery. Thus the two teacher model requests were candidate and screen calls, not two delivered treatments. The screened Hint said: “Your reproduction injects a tool-use event directly. Could you also trace whether the Anthropic provider can request and emit a delegation event in a real conversation? Compare its outgoing request and stream parsing with what the handler expects.” The second callback, at tool count 40, returned an empty Hint and did not add another server check. The delivered text is error-focused because it identifies a limitation of the reproduction, but it also uses exploratory, strategy-like questions rather than simply stating a correction. It is mixed guidance, not evidence about the other named variants. [Hint records, check 1; supplied online teacher events, checks 1–2.]

The delivered text entered actual student request index 7, ID `938686d71320456fbb18d5c60f55d6a8`, and appeared in nine requests. Entry establishes exposure in the request, not by itself behavioral adoption.

**Executable state transition.** Before the Hint, `main_agent` inspected `/app/backend/providers/anthropic.ts` (events 12, 16), and created a mock-provider reproduction that directly emitted `delegate_task`; the assertion that the child received `do work` failed (events 29–30). The agent then edited `/app/backend/handlers/multiAgentChat.ts`, `/app/backend/providers/types.ts`, and `/app/backend/providers/claude-code.ts` to introduce recursive execution, result continuation, and tool-use IDs (events 31–42). The teacher check occurred amid those edits, after the handler delegation edit and before the final continuation edit in the online event ordering.

After exposure, the agent identified the Anthropic provider gap (event 43). More importantly than that statement, events 46–56 show executable edits adding delegation history, an advertised tool schema, reconstructed tool-use/result messages, and parsing of streamed tool-use blocks in `/app/backend/providers/anthropic.ts`. Event 78 separately changed sub-agent error handling; event 79 disabled parallel tool use. These actions align with the Hint’s requested provider trace. The prior provider inspection and ongoing implementation mean the temporal sequence alone cannot establish that the Hint caused the changes. No actual live Anthropic conversation is shown.

**Local validation and commit.** The same mock reproduction subsequently passed (events 70–71 and 80–83), demonstrating the child-invocation assertion changed from failure to success; it did not itself verify real-provider behavior or the whole contract. Frontend/backend builds and backend typecheck eventually passed (events 70–71, 80–83). Earlier bundle failure was due to missing generated `cli/version.ts` (event 45); the subsequent backend build lacked frontend artifacts (event 69); and a test invocation duplicated `--run` (event 71). These are build-order or command failures, not demonstrated delegation-algorithm failures. The corrected local handler test had six passes and one abort-controller assertion failure (event 73; full tool record). The broader local suite had five failed tests and one unparseable OpenAI test suite; the causes of the screenshot failures are not established by the visible results (event 76 and full tool record). The agent removed the reproduction and committed four files as `717142e` on `recursive-agent-delegation` (events 90–91).

**Official result, separately.** The formal verifier applied a 35,809-byte patch and reported **F2P 7/7** and **P2P 31/31**, binary success and reward 1, exit code 0 and no timeout. Its stderr also contains a Node heap-out-of-memory message; despite that technical signal, the reported verifier grade is success, not evidence that every possible local or live-provider test passed. [Evaluation path above.]

## Candidate transferable lessons

A mock that injects a protocol event can establish handler behavior while leaving the actual event-producing provider untested. Separating callback, check, candidate, screen, delivery, request entry, and subsequent executable actions prevents overstating treatment exposure or response.

## Unverified hypotheses

The Hint may have accelerated attention to the provider boundary, but the pre-Hint inspection and lack of an intermediate-state replay prevent causal attribution. There is no independent Hint-to-knowledge transfer evaluation; formal success or differences in final grades alone do not measure learning value.
